explanations: login() looks the employee up by the normalized username (trimmed and lower-cased) but uses the raw string the client sent as the throttle key. Every spelling of the same username therefore gets its own failure counter, so an attacker can make unlimited guesses by rotating case or padding with spaces, and a locked account can still be signed into under another spelling. The fix normalizes once and uses that one key for the lock check, recording failures, resetting, and the directory lookup. The lockout then applies to the account identity, not the bytes that were typed.
